question: Where was India’s first wooden Gurdwara, Sri Nanak Niwas, constructed in Punjab in July 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fazilka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first wooden Gurdwara** in India, Sri Nanak Niwas, was constructed in **Fazilka**, Punjab, in **July 2025**.
 
• The initiative is a significant step in promoting **eco-friendly architecture** and preserving cultural heritage in India.
 
• Fazilka is a border district in Punjab and holds immense historical significance due to its **proximity to the India-Pakistan border**.
 
• Wooden Gurdwaras are rare in India due to traditional construction practices; this project stands out as a **unique blend of traditional Sikh architecture and sustainable materials**.
 
• This Gurdwara is dedicated to the teachings of **Guru Nanak Dev Ji**, the founder of Sikhism, and aims to attract devotees and tourists alike.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Fazilka:**

 
 
• Fazilka is known for its **rich cultural and historical importance** in Punjab.
 
• The district is famous for its **heritage buildings, traditional bazaars, and agricultural practices**.
 
• It serves as a key location for **cross-border trade and cultural exchanges** with Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Sri Nanak Niwas:**
 
 
• The Gurdwara is constructed using **sustainable wood**, which minimizes environmental impact compared to conventional construction materials.
 
• The design incorporates elements of **traditional Sikh architecture**, such as domes, arches, and intricate carvings.
 
• It also includes facilities for **community gatherings**, such as a langar hall and prayer rooms.
 
 
 
• **Eco-Friendly Construction:**
 
 
• Wooden structures are known for their **natural insulation properties**, which help in maintaining a comfortable indoor environment.
 
• The construction aligns with global trends of adopting **sustainable and renewable resources** in architecture.
 
• Wood is a **carbon-neutral material**, making it an environmentally friendly choice.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Wooden Gurdwaras:**
 
 
• Such structures symbolize a **return to traditional and natural construction practices**.
 
• They serve as an example of how **religious and cultural sites** can adopt sustainability without compromising on design and functionality.
 
• This project could inspire similar **eco-friendly religious structures** across the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Guru Nanak Dev Ji:**

 
 
• Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the **founder of Sikhism** and the first of the ten Sikh Gurus.
 
• He preached the message of **universal brotherhood, equality, and devotion to God**.
 
• The teachings of Guru Nanak emphasize the importance of **seva (selfless service)** and langar (community kitchen).
 
 
 
• **Eco-Friendly Religious Sites in India:**
 
 
• Several temples, mosques, and churches are adopting **green initiatives** such as solar power, rainwater harvesting, and eco-friendly construction.
 
• Examples include the **Golden Temple** in Amritsar, which uses renewable energy, and the **Lotus Temple** in Delhi, which emphasizes sustainable design.
